page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword at right foot, gathering signature at left foot. The left edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: momentum habet ea res etiam à naturalibus causis. Quippe duo sensus in nobis per quos Timor maximè in animum penetrat, Oculi & Aures. Alterutrum igitur illorum qui turbat, næ ille victoriæ suæ multum confert. Quid autem magis aures, quàm validus & magnus sonus? Itaque non iniuriâ Catoni Prisco hocCatonis dictum. adscribitur: Verba plus quam gladium, & voces quam manum, hostes territare & in fugam vertere. Sciuit Iosephus ille, & bonus dux, & scriptor, qui bello in Romanos, cùm morem eorum nosset occlamandi, metuens ne sui terrerentur: ἐκέλευσε πρὸς τὴν ἀλαλαγμὸν τῶν ταγμάτων ἀπορρῖψαι τὰς ἀκοὰς, ὡς μὴ καταπλαγῆναι:Lib. iii. cap. xviii. iussit ad clamorem legionum aures obstruere, ne percelleren-tur. Idque illi utiliter & suo bono fecerunt. Quid opus, si non violenta aliqua vis in istâ re? Itaque iam olim & aliæ vsæ gentes: idque Pane inuentore, ut vult Polyæ-nus. Is scribit, cùm Bacchus expeditione Indicâ in valle aliquâ cauâ cum copijs esset, ex aduerso autem infinita hostium multitudo, nonnihil in animo pertimuisse. Tum Panas suasisse, ut noctu Dionysij exercitus maximum clamorem tolleret, quem cum & petra & valles exceptum referrent & augerent, hostes territos in fugam se dediisse. Inde natum ut terrores eiusmodi Panici appellentur.Lib. 2. Strat. Imò verò Macedones & Persæ etiam vsi, de quibus ita Curtius: Jam in conspectu, sed extra teli iactum, utraque acies erat, cum priores Persæ inconditum & trucem sustinere clamorem. Reditur & à Macedonibus maior, exercitus impar numero, sed iugis montium vastisque saltibus repercussus.Lib. iii. Etiam Græci, quibus aut τ' ἀλαλάζειν passim tribuitur, aut τὸ παιανίζειν. Thucidides: ἐπεπαιώνισο αὐτοῖς ὡς Παιᾶν:

page.notes: The left margin shows the edge of the neighbouring page and has been left out. Uncertain readings: the page number "323" (the 3 looks like ʒ), the signature "s 2" (the first letter may be a long s or f), and several Greek words in the two lines after "ἐκέλευσε" and at the end of the Thucydides citation, where accents and letters are hard to read. The Greek "τ' ἀλαλάζειν" and "τὸ παιανίζειν" are read from a small, worn print. The Latin "Persæ" and "Reditur" are read as printed, with the hyphen between "Red-" and "ditur" not clearly visible. The Greek in the first line of the Thucydides citation is printed in italic.
